messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER: High tail latency and increased 5xx rate for public inference (region: us-east-1). Alerts from routing: sustained queueing on model shard gptx-6b-q4.

alice_sre: i'm on the page, pulling up logs and routing metrics

bob_oncall: joining, checking traffic heatmap and recent deploys

alice_sre: p95 for tier=free is spiking to ~1.2s, standard also affected. saw bursty qps from a few api keys (suspect ChatFlow Ltd). 5xx origin at runtime shard.

ryan_platform: quick thought: steer portion of low-tier traffic to lower-cost, less loaded model variant and throttle unauthenticated embedding requests. propose temporary smart-routing policy change + short rate limits.

jen_infra: can push policy changes. recommend canary 5% first.

alice_sre: plan: 1) apply tiered-steer policy canary (5%) -> observe p95 2) if good, roll to 40% 3) throttle unauthenticated embedding qps 80% 4) optional temporary quota bump for ChatFlow on dedicated pool to avoid outage.

anna_csm: ping - ChatFlow reported slower embeddings and occasional 502s. They're aware we're investigating; not yet critical outage but customer experience suffering.

bob_oncall: applying canary. Posting payload below for audit: 

```
POST /api/v1/routing/policies/apply
{
  "policy": "tiered-steer-emergency-2026-03",
  "rules": [
    {"match": "tier:free", "steer_to": "gptx-6b-q4a", "weight": 50},
    {"match": "tier:standard", "max_qps": 40}
  ],
  "canary_percent": 5,
  "reason": "reduce tail latency during us-east burst"
}
```

incident-bot: policy apply accepted (run_id: 8675309). Canary started at 5%.

bob_oncall: metrics @5m: canary p95 from 1.2s -> 0.62s on canary users. error rate down 30% for canary. proceeding to roll to 40% now.

ryan_platform: rolling to 40%. watching routing queue lengths and token cost. minor cost increase expected but within emergency thresholds.

alice_sre: also executing rate-limit for unauthenticated embeddings: 

```
/rl set --selector "auth:false" --limit 10r/s --duration 30m --reason "mitigate burst/unauthed spam"
```

jen_infra: throttle applied. confirming in dataplane.

anna_csm: update from ChatFlow: some requests faster, but intermittent failures persist for them. offered temporary dedicated capacity to keep latency stable.

alice_sre: initiate temporary quota bump for ChatFlow (cf-998) on dedicated pool to reduce client-facing errors while steering completes.

jen_infra: quota bump requested and approved; dedicated pool spinup queued. warmup ETA ~12 minutes. if we need faster, we can route that customer to eu-west fallback pool.

bob_oncall: canary -> 40% stable for 10m. cluster p95 improved ~22% overall, 5xx decreased notably. cost delta +3%.

alice_sre: marking incident P1 given customer impact and cross-team actions. paging infra lead for capacity and platform lead for routing rollback plan.

ryan_platform: added and instrumented a short-lived fallback rule: steerChatFlowToEU if dedicated warms > false, otherwise fallback to eu-west with tolerable latency delta. snippet: 

```
{ "fallback": { "match": "customer:cf-998", "route": "region:eu-west-1", "ttl": 900 } }
```

incident-bot: Incident escalated to P1. Pages sent to infra-lead and sla-oncall.

bob_oncall: preparing handoff in 30m. summary for handoff: applied policy tiered-steer-emergency-2026-03 (canary->40%), unauthenticated embedding throttle 10r/s 30m, temporary quota bump requested for cf-998, monitoring p95/5xx/cost. next: observe warm-up of dedicated pool or failover.

alice_sre: i'm compiling short timeline and customer-impact notes for postmortem. important action items: add conservative default steer for free tier under high-latency conditions; enforce stricter unauthenticated embedding quotas; add runbook for emergency routing policy rollbacks.

jen_infra: taking the handoff. i've confirmed policy state and rate limits, watching dashboards. if canary degrades, we'll rollback policy and immediately enable dedicated capacity for impacted customers.

bob_oncall: handing off to jen_infra now. i'll remain on-call reachable.

jen_infra: acknowledged. documenting timestamps and commands used in incident timeline channel. will keep monitoring until metrics stabilize. :eyes:
